_comment: What this harness assumes about Claude Code. upstream-check.sh compares these
assumptions against the installed CLI and fails when they stop being true.
acknowledged_hook_events is not 'events we use' — it is 'events a human has
looked at and made a decision about'. When upstream adds one, the check fails
until someone either hooks it or adds it here, which is the acknowledgement.
That is the mechanism that keeps the harness current instead of quietly stale.
acknowledged_surface does the same job for capabilities that are NOT hook
events: tools and settings keys. It exists because hook events were the only
thing the check could enumerate, so cross-session messaging — two tools and
two settings keys, shipped in 2.1.224 — landed while the check reported
'contract holds'. A checker's population is where things hide: anything
outside it reads as an all-clear.
READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING A GREEN RUN: acknowledged_surface is verified, not
discovered. `claude doctor` enumerates hook events, so section 4 can catch an
event nobody has seen. Nothing enumerates tools or settings keys, so section
4c can only confirm that what a human already wrote down still exists. A new
capability no one has noticed will not appear here on its own — that is a
standing limitation, and the check prints it rather than implying coverage.
Capability -> the decision a human made about it. Verified by substring
match against the CLI binary, which is advisory: a build could mangle a
string, so a miss is a prompt to check by hand, never a hard failure.

tools.SendMessage: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, not restricted. Cross-session messaging (2.1.224). Sends plain text to another of your sessions; it cannot approve a permission prompt or change config on the receiving side, so it does not widen this harness's blast radius. Deny it in permissions.deny to turn sending off.
tools.ListAgents: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, not restricted. Lists reachable sessions. Read-only, names and status only. Paired with SendMessage in any deny rule, since denying one without the other leaves a half-working surface.

settings_keys.crossSessionInbound: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, deliberately NOT set. With permissions.defaultMode 'auto' the receiving session counts as prompting, so inbound messages are delivered and a value would change nothing here. Left unset on purpose: an adopter running bypassPermissions gets holds instead, and that is the correct default for them. Revisit if this harness ever ships bypassPermissions.
settings_keys.isolatePeerMachines: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, deliberately NOT set. Requires approval before a message leaves the machine. Only meaningful with Remote Control connected, which this harness does not configure. Set it to true if this machine ever joins one.
settings_keys.dialogExpiry: Acknowledged 2026-08-27, deliberately NOT set. Governs how long a held inbound message waits for approval (default five minutes). The default is right for interactive use; a long-running `claude -p` worker wanting unattended delivery should set crossSessionInbound rather than stretch this.
settings_keys.subagentPromptCacheTtl: Acknowledged 2026-09-22, deliberately NOT set. Measured over 14 days of this machine's transcripts: main-session cache writes were all 1h (6,869), subagent writes all 5m (1,624). Only 4 of 1,614 subagent turns followed a gap over 5 minutes (303,618 tokens re-cached). Raising it would put every subagent write on the pricier 1h rate to save those 4. Revisit if the audit log's Agent lines show long-lived background subagents.
settings_keys.syncClaudeAiSkills: Acknowledged 2026-09-22 (2.1.275), NOT set, so skills enabled on the claude.ai account sync into terminal sessions. Open question for the owner: synced skills can carry inline shell commands that run under this machine's allow rules. Set false (with syncClaudeAiPlugins) to keep terminal skills to what is installed locally.
settings_keys.syncClaudeAiPlugins: Acknowledged 2026-09-22 (2.1.275), NOT set. Same decision and open question as syncClaudeAiSkills; change the two together.
settings_keys.maxEffortLevel: Acknowledged 2026-09-22 (2.1.267), NOT set. Caps effort for every model and subagent. The harness ships effortLevel xhigh and has no measurement that a cap would save anything without costing quality; revisit with the audit log's Agent lines.
settings_keys.bashEditDiffEnabled: Acknowledged 2026-09-22 (2.1.269), NOT set. Adds a diff of files a Bash command changed to its result. Useful but grows every such tool result; left to the user.
settings_keys.attribution: Acknowledged 2026-09-23 (2.1.281), NOT set. `false` hides all commit and PR attribution. The harness wants the co-author line (includeCoAuthoredBy true), and older CLIs skip a settings file holding the boolean form.

notes_on_unused_events.PermissionRequest: STRONG candidate, payload confirmed 2026-09-09: receives tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, permission_mode and effort, and returns {decision: allow|deny|ask, decisionReason}. With defaultMode auto the classifier resolves prompts a human used to see, so auditing its decisions would restore the lost record. Note the limitation: it fires where a permission DECISION is requested, so it is PermissionDenied below that carries the auto-mode denial.
notes_on_unused_events.PostCompact: Candidate: pre-compact.sh backs up the transcript; a post-compact counterpart could record what survived.
notes_on_unused_events.PermissionDenied: STRONGEST candidate, payload confirmed 2026-09-09: receives tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, denial_reason and permission_mode, and returns {retry}. This is the one gap that bit during this review: a session hit a classifier denial and audit.log recorded the attempt but NOT the verdict, so the friction census had to be reconstructed by re-deriving the matcher's rules over 40,346 logged commands instead of just reading the denials. Hooking this makes that measurement a lookup. Caveat: denial_reason is reportedly the fixed string 'Blocked by classifier' rather than a detailed explanation, so it identifies WHICH command was denied, not why.
notes_on_unused_events.PreModelSwitch: Acknowledged 2026-09-09, not adopted. Appeared between 2.1.250 and 2.1.266. Fires before a model switch is applied and CAN block it, returning permissionDecision allow/deny plus a reason. Not hooked: this harness does not police which model runs, and gating the model picker would be friction with no security gain. Revisit if model choice ever becomes a cost or compliance control.
notes_on_unused_events.PostModelSwitch: ADOPTED 2026-09-09 (audit.sh). Fires after a model switch; cannot block, returns systemMessage/additionalContext only. This entry first read 'not hooked, because audit.sh already records the tool calls either side of a switch, so the change is visible in the log' -- that was wrong and is kept here as the correction: every audit line is <ts> | <tool> | <target> | <dir> with no model field, so a switch left no trace whatsoever. For a long background session producing analysis, an unrecorded fallback silently changes the reliability of everything after it.
notes_on_unused_events.SubagentStart: Not adopted: subagent activity is already visible via PostToolUse.
notes_on_unused_events.UserPromptSubmit: Not adopted deliberately: it sees every prompt, which is the most privacy-sensitive surface in the harness.
notes_on_unused_events.TaskCreated: Not adopted: background-task lifecycle is not a security or continuity concern.
notes_on_unused_events.Setup: Not adopted: install.sh already owns first-run setup.
notes_on_unused_events.TeammateIdle: Not applicable to a single-developer harness.
notes_on_unused_events.Elicitation: Not adopted: MCP elicitation is out of scope (MCP is an explicit known limitation).
notes_on_unused_events.PostToolBatch: Not adopted: audit.sh already logs each tool call individually.
notes_on_unused_events.StopFailure: Candidate: would catch a Stop hook erroring, which currently fails silently.
notes_on_unused_events.InstructionsLoaded: Not adopted: CLAUDE.md loading is not audited.
notes_on_unused_events.CwdChanged: Not adopted: audit.sh already records cwd per entry.
notes_on_unused_events.DirectoryAdded: Candidate: --add-dir widens the file surface the guards protect.
notes_on_unused_events.FileChanged: Not adopted: external file changes are not the harness's concern.

upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn._comment: Reviewed 2026-08-12. If the harness duplicates one of these, delete the harness copy rather than maintaining two.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto-mode classifier: Adjudicates the permission prompts the guards' ask tier used to send to a human. See README 'Auto mode'.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.autoMode.{allow,soft_deny,hard_deny,envi: Native rule layer. VERIFIED 2026-09-09, replacing an earlier guess that read 'appears to replace the shipped defaults': a category set WITHOUT the literal string "$defaults" in its array does replace the entire default list for that section -- for soft_deny that discards every built-in soft block including force push, curl-pipe-bash, production deploys and auto-mode bypass; for hard_deny it discards the built-in data-exfiltration rule. Including "$defaults" splices the defaults in at that position, so entries can go before or after them. The harness shipping none was therefore the right call, but the reason is now a fact with a documented escape hatch rather than an assumption, so adding entries is safe PROVIDED "$defaults" is always present. autoMode.environment is prose describing which repos, buckets and domains are trusted, and is the documented lever for reducing classifier denials -- preferred over widening permissions.allow, because the two are independent gates: permissions is consulted first, the classifier second.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto-dream memory consolidation: Background memory hygiene with its own lock and rollback. See docs/memory-hygiene-research.md — do not rebuild it.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.shared/team memory sync: Server-side concurrent-write rejection, mass-delete guard, and secret scanning on memory writes.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.sandbox: OS-level containment; the real boundary the regex guards only approximate.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.symlink-aware native permission rules: 2.1.268 applies deny/ask rules to a path's real location and 2.1.280 judges writes by where they land. Overlaps sensitive-file-guard's symlink resolution. Keep the guard: it also covers Grep and reads that no shipped deny rule names.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.per-command allowed_domains: 2.1.271, auto mode with sandboxing only. Overlaps network-guard's domain allowlist, but the harness ships sandbox.enabled false, so it does not apply here.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Read/Edit deny on unanalyzable Bash line: Added in 2.1.268, REVERTED in 2.1.273: eval / env -C lines prompt again instead of being denied. The hole interpreter-guard and env-guard cover is open upstream; both stay.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Artifact tool vs WebFetch rules: 2.1.268: WebFetch deny/ask rules no longer apply to Artifact reads and publishes, and network-guard is matched on WebFetch only. Audited, not guarded: audit.sh logs Artifact, ArtifactData and ArtifactComments calls (action, url, ids, never content). Decide on a guard from that census. 2.1.281: artifact pages may also load scripts from unpkg.com; same census.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.auto mode and skill inline ! commands: 2.1.271: a skill's or slash command's inline ! commands follow permission rules, not the classifier. The shipped allow list includes broad entries (Bash(python3:*), Bash(node:*)), so such a command matching them runs without classifier review. Open question for the owner.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.Claude in Chrome per-site check in auto: 2.1.275: classifier-approved browser calls skip the extension's per-site check. No harness guard covers browser tools; the MCP audit census records them.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.recursive rm prompts in auto mode: 2.1.281: rm whose target is only command-substitution output (rm -rf "$(pwd)") now asks even with a Bash allow rule, and in auto mode the dangerous-rm prompt denies after 2 minutes with a rewrite hint. The shipped deny Bash(rm -rf:*) already refuses the literal form. Both opt-outs (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_SUBSTITUTION_RM_PROMPT, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DANGEROUS_RM_TIMEOUT) stay unset.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.server-side auto mode classifier: 2.1.281: where the classifier runs server-side, read-only and sandboxed shell commands also wait for it, and CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER now applies on a direct API connection. The PreToolUse guards run first either way. Not set.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.permission rules with a NUL byte: 2.1.281: such a rule now matches nothing instead of acting as a wildcard. No shipped rule has one.
upstream_features_that_overlap_this_harn.per-model effort on new models: 2.1.280: an effort level saved before /effort became per-model no longer applies to newly released models; they start at their default. Missed at the 2.1.280 review. Measured on this Mac 2026-09-23: Opus 5 messages ran xhigh, Opus 5.5 messages ran medium, despite effortLevel xhigh here. Fix per model with /effort; the status line now shows the live level.

_comment: The two thresholds that decide how much of MEMORY.md is loaded, read out of
the CLI rather than assumed. They were folklore here for a while: this repo's
own research doc recorded '~200-line index cap is unsubstantiated', while
memory-verify and memory-lint both enforced 200 as fact. Both turned out to
be right about the number and wrong about the confidence.
Upstream destructures {trimmed, lineCount, byteCount} and tests
lineCount > <lines> and byteCount > <bytes>. The size limit is BYTES -- the
identifier is literally byteCount -- which is why this harness reports bytes.
Truncation is line-first: the index is cut to <lines> lines, then clamped to
<bytes>, so passing line 200 drops everything after it.
Section 4d re-extracts both numbers by name, so a minifier rename cannot
strand the check the way a hardcoded identifier would.
